issues.explanation: Creating the entity plus owner membership is a domain write performed inline in the Livewire component, whereas the conventions require one app/Actions/* class per use case (authorizing inside it).

submit() persists data without $this->authorize('create', Entity::class); EntityPolicy::create is defined but never called, violating the non-negotiable Livewire rule that every public action authorizes server-side.
The custom current_entity middleware is not registered with Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware, so it silently stops applying on subsequent /livewire/update requests (Livewire security rule 6).
/home redirects to the already-picked entity's dashboard even when the user has more than one membership, whereas the task says >1 membership must always dispatch to the switcher.

With an empty session the landing dispatch returns before checking the route-bound entity, so a non-member requesting a dashboard is redirected to onboarding/switcher instead of receiving the 403 the dashboard requirement states.

pick() authorizes with a direct membershipFor() comparison rather than a policy/gate, and EntityPolicy has no corresponding ability, bypassing the project's rule that authorization always goes through policies.
Validation uses a rules() method instead of the project's documented #[Validate] attribute + $this->validate() pattern.

Onboarding tests cover validation, happy path and slug retry but not the required unauthorized direct call to submit() or a tamper attempt on the component state, and TenantContext population is never asserted.
The same Entities entry is added twice, including inside the already released [0.0.0] section.

review.summary: Adds the entities/entity_memberships data model with named unique indexes and the generated owner_seq constraint, models/factories/policies, tenant context and middleware, onboarding, dashboard, switcher, navbar link and a broad Pest feature suite. The task is largely met, but the Livewire creation action is written inline without an Action class or authorize() call, the custom tenant middleware is not persisted for Livewire updates, and two dispatch edge cases deviate from the spec, so the change needs rework before merging.
